[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne is a large scale data center provider headquartered in Dallas, Texas. In 2016 CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchanges original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly 130 million dollars, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15 year lease. In November 2021, KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately 15 billion dollar deal, taking the company private, and that acquisition closed in 2022. CyrusOne has operated as a privately held company since, a company level ownership fact this registry had not previously recorded with a citable source. This specific row is one of two entries in this registry both named PHX4, sitting roughly 350 meters apart, most likely representing a duplicate underlying map entity for the same building rather than two distinct facilities. A datacentermap listing dedicated to PHX4, fetched fresh this session, gives 2495 South Ellis Street, Building 1, Chandler, Arizona 85286 as the street address. This session applied the same confirmed address to both PHX4 rows and flags the duplication for a future researcher with parcel level or map editing access to merge or resolve.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX4 sits in Chandler, Arizona, as one building in a published 169 MW campus across eight facilities. The campus rank and published capacity for Arizona place this specific building below four other mapped sites in the state, none of which have disclosed individual facility specifications. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities total, of which only four publish megawatt figures to this registry.

The Chandler campus represents part of CyrusOne's portfolio as a privately held company following its 2022 acquisition by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners. The 2 million square foot building footprint at this address is confirmed from third-party mapping sources. No tenant occupancy, current utilization, power delivery topology, or grid interconnection details are published.

The facility's relevance to AI scaling depends on the unpublished portion of the 169 MW campus allocation and the state of Arizona's broader power position. With 512 MW of published data center capacity across the state and 52 additional mapped facilities publishing no figures, Arizona's actual AI infrastructure base remains largely undisclosed. The campus matters materially only if its allocation supports the density and cooling profiles required for current-generation accelerator workloads, a specification CyrusOne has not published.
